title: The High Cost of Low Range: Estimating the Hidden Cost of Range Anxiety in Electric Vehicles
Do Weight-Neutral Safety Ratings Curb the Vehicle Arms Race? Evidence from Safety Award Criteria Updates
abstract: Vehicle safety ratings are derived from controlled crash tests that hold vehicle weight fixed, effectively neutralizing weight as a factor in consumer safety information. This paper studies the tradeoff between providing more accurate information about real-world crash risk and the perverse incentives created when the true effects of weight are reflected in safety ratings. We isolate consumer preferences for top ratings from other vehicle characteristics by conditioning on the underlying crash test scores that determine each rating, and use those same scores as instruments to address selection concerns when linking safety ratings to realized outcomes in real-world collisions. We further exploit variation in opposing vehicle weight from two-car collisions to scale the empirical effects of a vehicle's relative weight on the road into a counterfactual safety rating. We find that incorporating weight into ratings strengthens incentives to purchase heavier vehicles, generating a strategic response of approximately 7 pounds per 100-pound increase in mean fleet weight. Back-of-the-envelope calculations imply that newly purchased vehicles would remain persistently heavier than the existing fleet, producing long-run external costs of up to $1.8 billion per model year. These findings suggest that maintaining weight-neutral, limited-information safety ratings may produce substantial social benefits by dampening the mechanism known as the vehicle "arms race."
abstract_zh: 车辆安全评级源自受控碰撞测试，这些测试固定了车辆重量，从而在消费者安全信息中有效地剔除了重量这一因素。本文研究了两者之间的权衡：一方面是提供更准确的实际碰撞风险信息，另一方面是当重量的真实影响反映在安全评级中时所产生的逆向激励。我们通过控制决定每个评级的基础碰撞测试分数，将消费者对最高评级的偏好与其他车辆特征区分开来，并以这些相同的分数作为工具变量，以解决将安全评级与实际碰撞结果相联系时的选择问题。我们进一步利用双车碰撞中对方车辆重量的变化，将车辆在路上相对重量的实证效应，换算为反事实的安全评级。我们发现，将重量纳入评级会强化购买更重车辆的激励，由此引发的策略性反应约为：车队平均重量每增加100磅，新购车辆重量增加约7磅。粗略的测算表明，新购车辆将持续比现有车队更重，每个车型年将产生高达18亿美元的长期外部成本。这些发现表明，维持与重量无关、信息有限的安全评级，可能会带来可观的社会效益，因为它能够抑制被称为车辆“军备竞赛”的机制。

title: Positive Spillovers from Infrastructure Investment: How Pipeline Expansions Encourage Fuel Switching
abstract: This paper studies the role of the U.S. pipeline infrastructure in the country's transition from coal to natural gas energy. I leverage the Environmental Protection Agency's Mercury and Air Toxics Standards as a plausibly exogenous intervention, which encouraged many coal plants to convert to natural gas. Combining this quasi-experimental variation with a plant's preexisting proximity to the pipeline network, I isolate implied pipeline connection costs within a dynamic discrete choice model of plant conversions. Key model results indicate that infrastructure-related costs prevent $9 billion in emissions reductions from taking place, suggesting a $2.4 million per mile external benefit of pipeline expansions.
abstract_zh: 本文研究了美国输气管道基础设施在该国从煤炭向天然气能源转型中的作用。我利用美国环境保护署的《汞与空气有毒物质标准》（MATS）作为一项看似外生的干预措施，该标准促使许多燃煤电厂转为使用天然气。我将这一准实验性变异与电厂原有的管道网络邻近程度相结合，在电厂转换的动态离散选择模型中分离出隐含的管道连接成本。关键模型结果表明，基础设施相关成本阻碍了90亿美元的减排实现，这表明管道扩建每英里可带来240万美元的外部收益。

title: Pounds that Save: The Role of Consumer Preferences for Safety in Demand for Large Vehicles
abstract: This paper provides novel evidence that consumers choose larger vehicles as an investment in their safety. I test for this purchasing behavior by isolating the quasi randomness of death in accidents involving at least one fatality. Leveraging this variation as a shock that made driving risk more salient to the victims’ acquaintances, I test whether consumers consequently infer a link between safety and vehicle weight. Using detailed information about household vehicle purchases and the locations of the purchasers’ residences, I demonstrate that households neighboring an individual who dies in an accident respond by purchasing significantly larger vehicles than comparable households neighboring someone who survives an accident. These findings capture strategic purchases of heavier vehicles for safety, behavior that can ultimately lead to the inefficiencies of a vehicle arms race.
abstract_zh: 本文提供了新的证据，表明消费者选择更大的车辆，是将其视为对自身安全的一种投资。我通过分离出涉及至少一人死亡的事故中的准随机死亡，来检验这一购买行为。利用这一变异作为一种冲击，它使驾驶风险在受害者的熟人中变得更加突出，我检验了消费者是否因此建立了安全与车辆重量之间的联系。利用家庭车辆购买的详细信息以及购买者住所的位置，我证明，与邻近交通事故幸存者的可比家庭相比，邻近交通事故中死亡者的家庭会购买显著更大的车辆。这些发现揭示了为安全而购买较重车辆的策略性行为，这种行为最终可能导致车辆军备竞赛的低效率。
